idiom_name: T | undefined under strictNullChecks with ?. and ??
implementation_notes: With strictNullChecks enabled, null and undefined stop being assignable to everything: they have distinct types, the union T | undefined is the option type, and the compiler's control-flow analysis narrows it (checks such as x !== undefined, early returns, ?. and ??). The tsconfig documentation states the contrast directly - without the flag the undefined case is erased from the type system and callers may assume a value that was never found. Types are erased at run time, so JSON payloads and casts are not covered; a hand-written discriminated union or a library Option (fp-ts O.Option with Some/None, map/flatMap/match/getOrElse, fromNullable/toUndefined for the boundary) covers the cases where absence must compose or be told apart from a stored undefined.
pitfalls: strictNullChecks is a compiler option: without it undefined is assignable to everything and the pattern simply does not exist, so the realization only counts with strict (or strictNullChecks) enabled and with `as` casts refused in review.
Types are erased: a value arriving as JSON is not a union until a schema parses it, and one cast turns 'possibly absent' into a lie the compiler then narrows confidently.
null and undefined are distinct: JSON has null, missing properties read as undefined, and APIs differ (find returns undefined, DOM lookups return null), so a boundary should normalize to one of them.
Optional properties and undefined-valued properties differ under exactOptionalPropertyTypes; the default configuration does not report the difference.

variants.name: fp-ts Option
variants.idiom_name: fp-ts Option<A> with some/none, map/flatMap and match
variants.implementation_notes: fp-ts defines Option<A> = None | Some<A> with none/some constructors, fromNullable/toUndefined/toNullable for the boundary, tryCatch for exception interop, and pipe-able map/flatMap/match/getOrElse; the module documentation presents it exactly as the effect of a possibly failing computation, contrasting a combinator pipeline with an imperative try/catch. Choose it where the code base already depends on fp-ts/Effect and absence must compose like other effects; the union-with-undefined realization stays the native default.
pitfalls: Two encodings of absence in one code base (undefined and Option) demand explicit conversions at each boundary; keep one convention per layer.
fp-ts is a dependency with its own vocabulary - adopting it for one function leaves the project with two idioms for the same outcome.
